paper_metadata.title: Quantum State Preparation by Improved MPS Method

experiments.description: Numerical evaluation of improved MPS (IMPS) amplitude preparation on three bounded-rank functions and three benchmark distributions, comparing MPS, TTN, HEN, and HTN connectivity schemes as qubit count increases.

algorithm.variant: Improved Matrix Product State (IMPS) amplitude preparation with parallel disentangling

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical functions/distributions are discretized into amplitudes of an n-qubit quantum state; the circuit approximately disentangles the target state to |0...0> and is reversed for preparation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state whose amplitudes approximate the target function/distribution; fidelity is evaluated against the original amplitude vector.

problem_instance.description: Amplitude preparation for three bounded-MPS-rank functions and three benchmark probability distributions over increasing qubit counts.

dataset_specification.description: Functions and distributions are analytically defined in the paper; random complex amplitudes are also tested as a separate scalability benchmark.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Target amplitudes are discretized over qubit registers; truncation/reset behavior differs by method (MPS/TTN reset after each layer; HTN/HEN reset after each U-depth).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Infidelity is computed as 1 - |<v|psi>|^2. Results are shown versus qubit number; for random amplitudes, each data point is averaged over 10 random samples.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 10-16 in plotted experiments; 12-qubit example highlighted; general n-qubit scaling discussed
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: O(log n) theoretical for IMPS; empirical U-depths 5, 10, and 11 reported

speedup_claims.conditions: without considering chip architecture / topological constraints
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states conventional MPS is O(n) depth and IMPS reduces this to O(log n); exact constants are not reported.

speedup_claims.factor: approximately (m + n)/2 depth; O(sqrt(N)) when m and n are comparable
speedup_claims.conditions: on an n x m grid chip with superconducting-style connectivity
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an architecture-specific scaling claim, not a measured runtime speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log n) circuit depth for IMPS; O(n) for conventional MPS; on an n x m grid chip, approximately (m + n)/2 depth is stated

experiments.description: Comparison of old versus optimized two-qubit unitary decomposition within IMPS, evaluating fidelity for randomly generated complex amplitudes across increasing qubit counts and multiple connectivity schemes.

algorithm.variant: Fourth-order unitary decomposition optimization using KAK/Cartan decomposition
algorithm.ansatz: Two-qubit unitary decomposition into single-qubit gates and CNOTs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Random complex amplitudes are loaded via MPS-style disentangling; the optimized fourth-order unitary replaces the original one in the same amplitude-preparation pipeline.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize infidelity of amplitude preparation while reducing two-qubit gate cost.

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated complex amplitudes used to test the optimized two-qubit unitary across problem sizes.

dataset_specification.description: Random complex amplitudes; averaged over 10 random samples per qubit count.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No additional preprocessing reported beyond random amplitude generation and normalization implicit in state preparation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Infidelity averaged over 10 random samples for each qubit count.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: up to 12 in the reported scalability discussion
quantum_resources.cnot_count: 2 for optimized unitary; 3 for original unitary

speedup_claims.factor: one-third reduction in two-qubit gate count
speedup_claims.conditions: for complex-valued amplitudes in the MPS amplitude-preparation pipeline
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims the optimized unitary uses 2 CNOTs instead of 3; no full circuit-depth benchmark is provided.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Two-CNOT implementation for the optimized fourth-order unitary; one-third reduction in two-qubit gate count relative to the three-CNOT baseline

experiments.description: Chip-topology adaptation experiment on a 3-row by 4-column grid, comparing traditional MPS and chip-adapted IMPS at different U-depths for the six target functions/distributions.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Amplitude preparation on a 3x4 superconducting-style grid topology using custom contraction/disentangling paths.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare target amplitudes with reduced circuit depth on constrained connectivity.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Topology-aware edge contraction / disentangling path on the grid.

problem_instance.description: Same six target functions/distributions evaluated on a 12-qubit grid-based chip example.

dataset_specification.description: 12-qubit example on a 3-row, 4-column grid; functions/distributions from the earlier experiment.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Amplitude reset at each U-depth for the chip-adapted method.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Infidelity comparison at U-depth 5 and 10 against traditional MPS at U-depth 11.

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: U-depth 5 and 10 for chip-adapted IMPS; U-depth 11 for traditional MPS

speedup_claims.conditions: on an n x m grid chip
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states that when m and n are comparable, this scales as O(sqrt(N)) for N = nm qubits.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: For an n x m grid chip, approximately (m + n)/2 circuit depth; when m and n are comparable, depth scales as O(sqrt(N)) for N = nm qubits
